title: Emergence of the magnetic octupole Rashba-Edelstein effect from spin-orbit entanglement
abstract: Magnetic multipoles have attracted growing interest as order parameters and dynamical degrees of freedom in unconventional magnets, yet it remains unclear how broadly they can emerge as active electronic degrees of freedom. Here, we show that spin-orbit-entangled multiorbital states can host magnetic octupole (MO) degrees of freedom. In Rashba systems, this gives rise to an MO Rashba texture accompanying the J-Rashba texture. Remarkably, spin-orbital entanglement can realize a pure-MO limit in which the spin and orbital-angular-momentum textures vanish while the MO texture remains finite. An applied electric field converts this texture into a nonequilibrium MO polarization through an MO Rashba-Edelstein effect. Around the pure-MO regime, the MO Edelstein response dominates over the conventional spin response, showing that multipolar responses need not be small corrections to dipolar spin physics. Our results establish an interface-based route for electrically generating nonequilibrium multipolar magnetic polarization in spin-orbit-coupled systems.
summary: This work demonstrates that magnetic octupole (MO) degrees of freedom can emerge robustly in spin-orbit-entangled multiorbital systems. It establishes the MO Rashba-Edelstein effect, showing that an applied electric field can generate a non-equilibrium MO polarization. This MO response can be dominant and provides a novel, electrically controllable mechanism for manipulating magnetic order in antiferromagnets.
main_problem: The paper investigates the emergence and electrical generation of magnetic octupole (MO) degrees of freedom in electronic systems, particularly in the context of Rashba-Edelstein effects.
main_result: Spin-orbit-entangled multiorbital states can host MO degrees of freedom, leading to an MO Rashba-Edelstein effect that can dominate over conventional spin responses, providing an interface-based route for generating non-equilibrium MO polarization.
method: Theoretical analysis using minimal models for $p$-orbitals on a 2D lattice, calculating non-equilibrium polarization via linear response theory (e.g., $\delta\langle D_y angle = \chi_D E_x$).
model_or_system: The study uses spin-orbit-entangled multiorbital states, modeled by $p_x, p_y, p_z$ orbitals on a 2D triangular or square lattice, incorporating SOC and interface-induced splitting.
key_observables: MO Rashba texture, MO Rashba-Edelstein polarization ($\delta\langle O_y angle$), Néel MO torque ($T_{MO}$), and sublattice-resolved susceptibilities ($\chi^D_{A,B}$).
important_parameters: Pure-MO limit, $d$-wave Antiferromagnet (AM) structure, and the relative strength of MO vs. spin responses.
main_assumptions: The analysis often employs the constant-relaxation-time intraband approximation for non-equilibrium responses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the emergence of MO textures, the pure-MO limit, and the calculation of current-induced torques on the Néel vector, showing MO accumulation dominating spin accumulation in certain bands.
paper_structure: The paper develops from general concepts of magnetic multipoles in spin-orbit-entangled systems to specific models (triangular/square lattice) demonstrating the MO Rashba texture, and finally applying this to calculate a measurable torque in $d$-wave antiferromagnets.
why_interesting: The focus on multipolar responses (octupoles) and their electrical generation via the Edelstein effect is highly relevant to understanding emergent magnetic order and spin-orbit torque mechanisms in modern spintronics and topological materials.
